If boiling is impossible, add 8 drops (1/8 teaspoon) of fresh, unscented household liquid chlorine bleach (approx. 6% sodium hypochlorite) per gallon of clear water, stir thoroughly, and allow to stand for 30 minutes before consuming.

query: When defending property against an approaching wildfire ember storm, what immediate actions reduce structure ignition before evacuating?
expected_facts: Embers entering open windows, vents, or igniting outdoor furniture cause over 70% of wildfire home ignitions.
ground_truth_answer: 1. Close all windows, doors, pet flaps, and skylights to block flying embers. 2. Move lightweight combustible patio cushions, deck furniture, door mats, and firewood piles indoors or at least 30 feet from the structure. 3. Shut off residential propane tanks and natural gas mains. 4. Leave exterior lights on so first responders can navigate through heavy smoke, then evacuate along designated corridors.

query: A confirmed EF-4 tornado is approaching a suburban area in 5 minutes. A resident lives in a manufactured/mobile home. Where should they seek shelter?
expected_facts: Mobile homes offer zero protection against tornado winds and must be abandoned immediately.
Seek a sturdy permanent building, reinforced tornado shelter, or as a last resort, lie flat in a low-lying ditch covering your head.
ground_truth_answer: Immediately abandon the mobile/manufactured home. Mobile homes cannot withstand tornado winds and are easily overturned. Run to a designated underground storm shelter or nearby permanent, substantial masonry building. If no sturdy structure is accessible within minutes, lie flat face-down in a low-lying ditch or ravine away from vehicles, covering your head and neck with your arms.

query: After a hurricane passes, an energized high-voltage power line has fallen across a vehicle with two passengers trapped inside. What should the passengers do?
expected_facts: Stepping out of an energized vehicle creates a path to ground, resulting in fatal electric shock.
Passengers must stay inside until the power utility confirms lines are de-energized.
ground_truth_answer: Passengers must stay inside the vehicle. The rubber tires insulate the car; as long as occupants do not touch the ground and car simultaneously, they are protected. Call 911 and wait for utility crews to de-energize the line. Only if the vehicle catches fire should passengers exit: jump completely clear of the car without touching it and ground at the same time, landing with both feet together, and bunny-hop away.

query: Is the St. Vrain Creek at Lyons river gauge currently indicating major flood conditions requiring immediate valley evacuation?

query: During an extreme heat wave with heat indices reaching 115°F and rolling blackouts, what are the primary warning signs of life-threatening heat stroke versus heat exhaustion?
expected_facts: Heat stroke is marked by core temp >103°F, altered mental state, confusion, hot dry or damp skin, and loss of consciousness.
Heat stroke is a medical emergency requiring immediate 911 intervention and aggressive active cooling.
ground_truth_answer: Heat stroke is an immediate life-threatening emergency. Distinguishing signs include: core body temperature above 103°F, altered mental state, confusion, slurred speech, delirium, seizures, or loss of consciousness, with hot, flushed, dry skin or profuse sweating. In contrast, heat exhaustion presents with heavy sweating, cold pale clammy skin, dizziness, and nausea with normal cognition. For suspected heat stroke, call 911 immediately and initiate rapid external immersion/ice cooling.

query: Following 72 hours of torrential rain in a steep mountain burn scar, what audio and visual clues indicate an imminent debris flow or mudslide?
expected_facts: A faint rumbling that increases in volume like a freight train, cracking trees, and sudden muddy stream discharges signal imminent debris flow.
ground_truth_answer: Key imminent warning signs of a debris flow include: a low, persistent rumbling noise that steadily intensifies (often compared to an approaching freight train), sounds of cracking boulders and snapping timber, sudden changes in water clarity from clear to murky or muddy torrents, sudden drops in streamflow (indicating upstream debris damming), and tilted trees or telephone poles on hillsides. Immediately evacuate uphill and away from stream channels.

query: What documentation steps are required by FEMA and insurers before homeowners discard flood-damaged drywall, carpet, and appliances?
expected_facts: Photograph the exterior and interior, including the clear high-water mark line, before discarding items.
Record serial numbers, make, and model of all major appliances and save a 1-foot square swatch of carpet.
ground_truth_answer: Before removing or discarding any flood-damaged building materials or contents: 1. Take extensive high-resolution photos and video of every room, specifically capturing the visible high-water mark lines on walls. 2. Photograph appliance model plates and serial numbers. 3. Cut and preserve a 1-square-foot sample of damaged carpet and pad for the adjuster. 4. Maintain a detailed written inventory of every item discarded with estimated purchase dates and costs.

query: The Air Quality Index (AQI) from wildfire smoke has spiked to 320 (Hazardous). Do cloth bandanas or surgical masks filter toxic PM2.5 particulates?
expected_facts: Cloth masks, bandanas, and standard loose surgical masks do not filter fine microscopic PM2.5 wildfire particulates.
Only well-fitted NIOSH-certified N95, KN95, or P100 respirators effectively reduce particulate inhalation.
ground_truth_answer: No. Cloth bandanas, scarves, and standard paper surgical masks do not trap hazardous microscopic PM2.5 smoke particulates because they lack electrostatic filtering media and seal edges. Only properly fitted, NIOSH-approved N95 or P100 particulate respirators effectively capture PM2.5 particles. Individuals in Hazardous AQI zones should remain indoors with HEPA air filtration.

query: A highway transport tanker displaying DOT UN 1075 with a red flammable gas diamond is overturned and hissing. What is the minimum initial evacuation distance?
expected_facts: UN 1075 identifies liquefied petroleum gases (propane/butane).
DOT Emergency Response Guidebook specifies an initial isolation distance of 100 meters (330 feet) and 1/2 mile (800 meters) in all directions if tank is involved in fire/leak.
ground_truth_answer: UN 1075 indicates Liquefied Petroleum Gases (propane/butane). Per the DOT Emergency Response Guidebook (Guide 115), immediately isolate the area for at least 100 meters (330 feet) in all directions for a spill or leak. If a bulk container is leaking or impinged by fire, expand the immediate evacuation perimeter to 1/2 mile (800 meters or 2,600 feet) in all directions due to catastrophic Boiling Liquid Expanding Vapor Explosion (BLEVE) risk.

query: Under the Simple Triage and Rapid Treatment (START) protocol at a mass-casualty building collapse, what tag color is assigned to an unconscious victim with a respiratory rate of 38 breaths per minute?
expected_facts: Under START triage, any spontaneous breathing rate over 30 breaths per minute immediately classifies the casualty as Red (Immediate).
ground_truth_answer: Red Tag (Immediate priority). Under the adult START triage algorithm, if a patient is breathing spontaneously and their respiratory rate exceeds 30 breaths per minute (tachypnea), triage assessment ceases and they are immediately assigned a Red/Immediate category requiring emergency transport and stabilization.

query: A motorist is stranded in their passenger car in rural Wyoming during a severe blizzard with whiteout conditions and 4-foot snowdrifts. Should they leave the vehicle on foot to seek help?
expected_facts: Never abandon a vehicle in a blizzard as disorientation and fatal hypothermia occur within minutes in whiteouts.
Keep the exhaust tailpipe clear of snow drifts when running the engine 10 minutes per hour for heat to avoid CO poisoning.
ground_truth_answer: Stay inside your vehicle. Do not attempt to walk through a blizzard. In whiteout conditions, distance and direction are lost within yards, leading to rapid disorientation and fatal hypothermia. Your car provides shelter and makes you visible to search crews. Tie a bright cloth to the antenna or door handle, run the engine and heater for only 10 minutes per hour to conserve fuel, and ensure the exhaust tailpipe is completely free of snow buildup to prevent deadly carbon monoxide poisoning.
